title: Justice for daily wage earner: SC awards Rs. 225,000 for police abuse
byline: While awarding Rs. 225,000 in compensation to a daily wage earner for unlawful arrest, detention and torture by three policemen attached to the Hanwella Police Station in 2023, the Supreme Court held that the Constitution does not permit law enforcement authorities to treat individuals differently based on prejudice or social profiling, particularly on account of their poor economic status.

title: TPA secures direct Presidential mechanism for hill country Tamil issues
byline: A high-level meeting between President Anura Kumara Dissanayake and the Tamil Progressive Alliance (TPA), led by MP Mano Ganesan, has resulted in a key administrative step aimed at addressing issues faced by the Indian-origin Malayaha Tamil community.

title: Russian oil unlikely anytime soon
byline: Sri Lanka is unlikely to secure a shipment of Russian oil anytime soon, as logistical arrangements are still under discussion while the one-month US sanctions waiver is due to expire on April 11, the Daily Mirror learns.

title: Expert committee appointed to restructure National Colleges of Education
byline: An expert committee has been appointed to enhance standards and restructure the National Colleges of Education, with a focus on producing a new generation of competent and transformative teachers.

title: Foreign cybercrime suspects to face Sri Lankan law, no immediate deportation: Police
byline: Amid a rising number of foreign nationals allegedly involved in cybercrime and online scams in Sri Lanka, police said that offenders will be prosecuted under the country’s Cybercrimes Act and will not be immediately deported or allowed to leave the country.

title: What do astronauts eat on the way to the Moon? Inside the Artemis II menu
byline: ASA’s ambitious Artemis II mission, which launched on April 1, is sending four astronauts on a historic 10-day journey around the Moon aboard the Orion spacecraft.

title: Scheduled water cuts continue in Colombo district
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) announced that the scheduled water cuts affecting several areas in the Colombo District due to prevailing dry weather conditions will continue today (April 04).

title: A-10 aircraft hit by Iranian air defenses, second US aircraft to go down in Middle East
byline: A U.S. A-10 aircraft has been hit by Iranian air defenses, Iranian state media reported, citing Iran’s Army public relations office.

title: Coal issue: Chanaka accuses Minister of suppressing report
byline: SLPP MP D.V. Chanaka has accused Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody of attempting to suppress a report on the importation of substandard coal.

title: Hot weather to continue despite rains in some areas: Met. Department
byline: The Department of Meteorology said yesterday that the hot weather will continue throughout April despite rains being forecast in some areas in the country.

title: Greek PM reshuffles cabinet as EU aid farm fraud probe widens
byline: ATHENS, April 3 (Reuters) - Greek Prime ​Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis reshuffled his cabinet on Friday, as he seeks to limit ‌the fallout from a growing scandal over alleged fraud related to European Union farm funds.

title: Government to test online work for public service on April 16 - 17
byline: The Ministry of Public Administration informed that examinations, including the Grama Niladhari entrance examination were conducted as planned.

title: Thundershowers with severe lightning expected
byline: Thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely to occur in several parts of the country after 1.00 p.m. today, the Meteorology Department said.

title: Iran, US race to recover missing crew member of crashed American fighter jet
byline: Iranian and American forces raced each other Saturday to recover a crew member of the first US fighter jet to go down inside Iran since the start of the war.

title: Indian art record: Ravi Varma painting fetches $17.9m
byline: A 19th-century masterpiece by Raja Ravi Varma has sold for a record $17.9 million at an auction in Mumbai, setting a new benchmark for Indian art and underscoring its growing global value.

title: Water levels low at Kalatuwawa and Labugama
byline: The capacity of Kalatuwawa and Labugama reservoirs have been fast swindling due to the prolonged dry weather. The water supply to Colombo and its suburbs depend on these two reservoirs. This has resulted in intermittent water cuts to manage the situation. National Water Supply and Drainage Board has requested consumers to use water sparingly.

title: Omani, French and Japanese vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz
byline: A French container ship, three Oman-linked tankers and a Japanese-owned gas carrier have crossed ⁠⁠the Strait of Hormuz, as some vessels make the passage through the contested waterway.

title: Petrol price drops to Rs378 as Pakistan PM cuts levy amid backlash
byline: ISLAMABAD: Just a day after an unprecedented surge in petroleum prices, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday announced a major relief measure, slashing the petroleum levy by Rs80 per litre and bringing the price of petrol down to Rs378 per litre.

title: Reduce taxes, tariff; Opposition MPs tell IMF
byline: Opposition MPs who met the visiting IMF delegation at the parliamentary complex requested them to intervene in getting the Sri Lankan government to grant tax and tariff cuts.

title: Food prices spiked in March as Middle East conflict drove up energy costs
byline: Food prices rose sharply in March as war in the Middle East drove up energy prices and freight costs around the world, a UN report says.

title: Afternoon showers expected across island
byline: Showers or thundershowers are expected in most parts of the island after 1.00 p.m. today, according to the weather forecast issued at 5.30 a.m.

title: Over Rs. 6 million spent to train a doctor: Minister
byline:
The government spends more than Rs. 6 million of public tax money to produce a single doctor, Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment 
Minister, Upali Pannila said today.

title: NWSDB to further trim duration of water cuts in Colombo areas
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced plans to further shorten the duration of scheduled water cuts in several areas across Colombo.

title: Venerable Dr. Kirinde Assaji Thera honoured with lifetime achievement award in UK
byline: Venerable Dr. Kirinde Assaji Thera has been awarded a Lifetime Achievement Award by Canterbury Christ Church University in recognition of his global spiritual leadership and decades of community service.

title: Indian buying Iranian crude without any payment hurdle
byline: Indian refiners are buying crude from Iran as part of their efforts to secure oil supplies amid the disruption in energy flows due to the West Asia war and there are no payment-related hurdles in paying for Iranian oil, the government said Saturday.

title: ‘1990 Suwa Seriya’ opens new head office in Colombo
byline: The new head office of the 1990 Suwa Seriya Foundation was officially inaugurated today (April 4) under the patronage of Health and Media Minister Nalinda Jayatissa.

title: Sajith did attend Gammanpila’s book launch
byline:
Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa did attend the launch of the book 
’Searching for the Mastermind of the Easter Sunday Attacks’ written by former Minister Udaya Gammanpila, MP Mujibur Rahman confirmed today.

title: GMOA strike baseless, no room for talks – Minister
byline: The strike launched by the Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) over the appointment system for doctors who have completed their internship has no basis for discussion, Minister of Health and Mass Media Nalinda Jayatissa said.

title: Trump warns Iran has 48 hours to reopen Strait of Hormuz
byline: US President Donald Trump recalls his twice-delayed threat to bomb Iran’s energy sites if it doesn’t open the Strait of Hormuz, which expires on Monday.
